Definition: an Achiramite or descendant (collectively) of Achiram
BiblicalUsage: The Ahiramites were the family named for Ahiram, counted among the sons of Benjamin in the second census — the word is not a man's name but a family's. The clan is traced through Ahiram, whose name stands in the same census verse.
TheologicalSignificance: A family name in a census carries no doctrine. It is one of the many threads the Bible keeps to show that Israel was not a crowd — it was families, counted by name.
